title: POP safety gradient: p50/p95-aware region routing with network-health scoring & model-variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a production-ready region selection policy that blends short-term latency percentiles (p50/p95) with an independently computed network health score to make tier-aware routing decisions and trigger graceful fallback to compatible model variants. The new policy should reduce p95 tail exposure during transient network degradation while preserving p50 latency-optimal paths where appropriate. It must integrate with the existing telemetry pipeline, Console dashboards, and rollout/feature-flag system.

Background: Current region selection uses static affinity + p50 sliding-window heuristics. We see tail spikes that correlate with packet loss and path variability; these spikes cause customer-facing latency regressions and higher error rates when large batches cross degraded links. We want a single, auditable decision path that: combines percentile-based latency signals, a packet-loss/jitter-derived network health score, and tier penalties to decide the preferred POP and a ranked fallback list (including model-variant fallbacks).

Acceptance criteria:
- New policy computes a composite score per POP every 15s: composite = weighted(p95_norm, p50_norm, network_health_norm, tier_penalty).
- p50 and p95 derived from the same sliding window (5m, 10s granularity) and smoothed with EWMA (alpha=0.25) for stability.
- Network health score combines packet loss, TCP retransmit rate, and 1s probe latency jitter into a 0-100 score using z-score normalization and temporal decay.
- Policy exposes per-POP signals to Console (rank list, composite score, contributing signals) and a new dashboard with alerting rules.
- Fallback mapping: when composite score > threshold_high, prefer fallback variants in order: quantized-medium -> quantized-small -> region-remote-large (explicit mapping file).
- Rollout: behind feature flag; start with 2% canary traffic in EU/NA, monitor defined metrics for 48h before scaling to 25% and full roll out if no regressions.

Technical approach summary:
1) Telemetry ingestion: extend the telemetry transformer (ingest-latency-service) to emit p50/p95 per POP per model-tuple every 10s (5m sliding window). Persist ephemeral time-series to the region-routing store (redis-timeseries) with TTL 1h.
2) EWMA smoothing service: new lightweight smoothing worker will subscribe to the timeseries stream and maintain smoothed p50/p95. This separates noisy raw percentiles from policy decisions.
3) Network health scorer: a small stateless function that fuses packetloss, retransmit_rate, and jitter into a normalized score using rolling z-scores and exponential decay (half-life 60s). The function publishes nethealth per POP with metadata for tracing.
4) Composite scorer and ranker: server-side policy in routing service (region-orchestrator) calculates final composite score. Weights default to {p95:0.5, p50:0.2, nethealth:0.25, tier_penalty:0.05} and are configurable per customer tier.
5) Fallback variant resolver: look up model compatibility matrix (in config service). If a top-ranked POP's composite crosses thresholds, the resolver will pick fallback variants in order and add them to the request plan with per-variant routing hints.
6) Circuit breakers & hysteresis: implement a cooldown window (3m) before a POP can be re-promoted; add minimum promotion delta on composite score to prevent oscillation.

Operational plan:
- Dashboards: routing-composite-scores, per-pop p50/p95 heatmap, nethealth trends, fallback-activation events.
- Alerts: (1) composite_score_drop > 15 for >= 1m on >=2 POPs; (2) fallback rate > 1% for production customers with >10 TPS.
- Rollback conditions: error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or median latency regressions > 10% in canary cohort for 30m.

Dependencies and links:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/smart-routing/pop-safety-gradient (design v1.2)
- Telemetry infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482
- Routing service RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Routing/Composite+Scorer+RFC
- Model-compatibility matrix: https://config.redwood.com/model-compat/matrix.csv
